subtitle: Pot beans with epazote
verso: Where one can eat, two can eat.
story: The pot that's always on grandma's stove. Pintos and bayos in the north; bayos, flor de mayo and peruanos as much as black in the center; black beans in the south and along the Gulf. All of them cooked slowly with onion, lard and epazote. The broth matters as much as the beans.

ingredients.title: Beans
items: 1 lb dried pinto or black beans

steps: Spread the beans on a tray and pick out stones and broken beans. Rinse well.
Put the beans, water, onion, garlic and lard in a heavy pot (a lead-free clay olla if you have one). Bring to a boil.
Lower to a gentle simmer, partly covered, for 1½–2 hours. If you need more water, add hot water only. Cold water toughens the skins.
When the beans are soft, add the salt and epazote. Simmer 30 minutes more so the salt gets in.
Serve in bowls with their broth, chopped onion, cilantro, serrano and queso fresco, or use them for refried beans.

pressureCooker.time: 45 min high pressure + full natural release
steps: Rinse and pick over the beans. No soaking needed.
Put the beans, [[8 cups]] water, onion, garlic and lard in the pot.
High pressure 45 minutes for pintos, 35 for black beans (10–12 if soaked overnight). Let the pressure release naturally, about 25 minutes.
Add the salt and epazote and simmer on Sauté 10–15 minutes.
pressureCooker.note: Don't fill past the halfway line with beans and water. Beans foam.

tips: Salt goes in after the beans are soft.
Clay ollas give the best beans, but buy ones marked Sin Plomo (lead-free). Old or unmarked glazes can leach lead.
Old beans take forever. Buy them where a lot of people buy beans.

variations.name: Frijoles Refritos
variations.subtitle: Refried beans
variations.note: Fried once, in plenty of lard. Refritos means well-fried, not fried twice.

items: 4 cups cooked beans plus 1 cup of their broth
3–4 tbsp lard (or bacon or chorizo fat)

steps: Heat the lard in a wide skillet and fry the onion until golden. Take the onion out if you like.
Add the beans and broth and mash with a bean masher as they cook.
Keep cooking and stirring about 10 minutes, until thick enough to hold a line when you drag a spoon through. Add broth if it gets too thick.

variations.name: Frijoles Charros
variations.subtitle: Cowboy beans
variations.note: For carne asada Sundays. In Monterrey, chicharrón goes in at the end. Add a beer and some call them frijoles borrachos; families argue about where one ends and the other begins.

items: 6 cups pinto pot beans with their broth
2 hot dogs and 2 slices ham, chopped
½ onion, 2 tomatoes and 2 jalapeños, chopped

steps: Fry the bacon until crisp. Add the chorizo, then the hot dogs and ham, and brown.
Add the onion, tomato and jalapeño and cook 5 minutes.
Add the beans with their broth (and the beer). Simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and the chicharrón right before serving.
variations.pressureNote: Cook the beans under pressure as in the base, then finish on Sauté.
